- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope downward by 0.5–1.0 units per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out forecast curve using 5-day moving average if sentiment volatility > 0.33.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.67, -0.00), model often misaligns with true trend; align forecast midpoint with sentiment average over last 5 days.
